meanings.usage: 不可数名词，指对信息保密的行为或状态
不可数名词，指产生预期结果的能力
作“氛围”讲时可作可数或不可数名词，指周围的整体环境和感觉
指为获取信息或真相进行的询问或研究
常见搭配engage in sth. 表示“从事/参与某事”；be engaged in表示“忙于，从事于”
用于修饰形容词或动词，表示程度大
用于描述事物最核心、最重要的部分
可修饰抽象名词，表示好的、有利的性质
工业领域常指生产工艺，也可泛指事情发展的过程
take out a patent为固定搭配，意为“取得专利”

meanings.meaning: 专利权（指对发明创造的专属使用权
也可作动词表示“获得专利”） verb. 获得专利权

meanings.usage: 与机器、机械相关的，也可指行为机械呆板的
商务领域常指代理商，文中指商业情报人员
指通过线索找到人或事物的来源、行踪
常接task, project, research等名词，表示承担某项工作

phrases.usage: 表示“严重不利于；对…有很大负面影响”，主语通常为不利因素，宾语为受影响的事物

examples.en: Lack of funding weighs heavily against the development of small businesses.
examples.zh: 资金短缺严重不利于小企业的发展。

examples.en: His lack of experience weighs heavily against his chance of getting the job.
examples.zh: 他经验不足，这对他获得这份工作的机会非常不利。

phrases.usage: 连词短语，意为“在…范围内；就…而言”，用于引导状语从句，限定论述的范围

examples.en: In so far as you are a student, you should obey the school rules.
examples.zh: 作为学生，你应该遵守校规。

examples.en: I will help you in so far as I can.
examples.zh: 我会尽我所能帮助你。

phrases.usage: 动词短语，意为“从事；参与”，可用于主动或被动语态be engaged in

examples.en: Many college students engage in part-time jobs during holidays.
examples.zh: 很多大学生假期会从事兼职工作。

examples.en: He is engaged in scientific research on environmental protection.
examples.zh: 他正从事环境保护方面的科学研究。

phrases.usage: 固定搭配，意为“取得专利权”，指为发明申请并获得专利保护

examples.en: The company decided to take out a patent for its new invention.
examples.zh: 这家公司决定为它的新发明申请专利。

examples.en: It took them three years to take out a patent on this new energy technology.
examples.zh: 他们花了三年时间才取得这项新能源技术的专利。

phrases.usage: 此处意为“适用于；针对”，主语为规则、情况等，宾语为适用的对象

examples.en: This regulation applies to all employees, regardless of position.
examples.zh: 这条规定适用于所有员工，不分职位高低。

examples.en: The discount only applies to products purchased before the end of the month.
examples.zh: 这个折扣仅适用于月底前购买的产品。

phrases.usage: 意为“到如此程度以至于”，用于强调程度，引导结果状语从句

examples.en: The noise from the construction site was loud to such an extent that we couldn't sleep at night.
examples.zh: 工地的噪音大到我们晚上根本睡不着觉。

examples.en: He was absorbed in the book to such an extent that he didn't hear the doorbell.
examples.zh: 他看书太入迷了，以至于都没听到门铃声。

phrases.usage: 连词短语，意为“生怕；唯恐”，引导目的状语从句，从句常用虚拟语气

examples.en: She locked the door for fear that someone might break in while she was out.
examples.zh: 她锁了门，生怕自己出门的时候有人闯进来。

examples.en: He left an hour early for fear he might miss the train.
examples.zh: 他提前一小时出发，唯恐赶不上火车。

grammar.title: 定语从句的省略结构
grammar.structure: 句子1, + 名词/代词 + 其他成分（省略与前文重复的主语+be/谓语动词）
grammar.definition: 在并列结构中，当第二个分句的主语和谓语与前一分句的主语和be动词相同时，可以省略主语和be动词，仅保留剩余成分 常用于对比、列举两个并列的因素、情况，使句子更简洁凝练，避免重复

examples.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry. One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out, the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
examples.zh: 有两个因素严重地妨碍着工业中科学研究的效率：一是科研工作中普遍存在的保密气氛，二是研究人员缺乏个人自由。

examples.en: There are two rooms in the apartment. One is used as a bedroom, the other as a study.
examples.zh: 这套公寓有两个房间，一个用作卧室，另一个用作书房。

grammar.title: such...that...引导的结果状语从句
grammar.structure: such + (a/an) + 形容词 + 可数名词单数/不可数名词/可数名词复数 + that 从句
grammar.definition: 用于表示“如此…以至于…”，强调程度，引出前文动作或状态带来的结果 当修饰的中心词是名词时用such，若修饰形容词或副词则用so，that引导的从句表示结果

examples.en: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
examples.zh: 某些大公司进行的研究属于一般性和基础性的研究，因此不保密对它们反而更有好处。

examples.en: It was such a cold day that we decided to stay at home.
examples.zh: 天气太冷了，我们决定待在家里。

grammar.title: 状语从句中的虚拟语气
grammar.structure: 主句 + for fear that / lest / in case + 主语 + should + 动词原形
grammar.definition: 在for fear that, in case, lest等引导的目的状语从句中，常用“should + 动词原形”的虚拟语气结构，表示担忧的、可能性较小的情况 用于表达“生怕、以防、唯恐”的含义，should可以省略，尤其在口语和非正式文体中

examples.en: Many firms, for instance have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
examples.zh: 例如，许多公司很难从图书馆借到技术或科学书籍，因为它们不愿意让自己的名字被登记为借了某某类书籍，生怕其他公司的情报人员能够据此推断出他们可能正在进行的研究类型。

examples.en: She put the umbrella in her bag for fear that it should rain in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 她把伞放进包里，以防下午下雨。

patterns.pattern: Two factors weigh heavily against... One is..., the other...

original.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry. One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out, the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
original.zh: 有两个因素严重地妨碍着工业中科学研究的效率：一是科研工作中普遍存在的保密气氛，二是研究人员缺乏个人自由。

imitations.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the popularity of the new product. One is its high price, the other its complex operation.
imitations.zh: 有两个因素严重影响这款新产品的普及：一是价格过高，二是操作复杂。

imitations.en: Two factors weigh heavily against students' learning efficiency. One is the lack of clear learning goals, the other the distraction of electronic devices.
imitations.zh: 有两个因素严重影响学生的学习效率：一是缺乏明确的学习目标，二是电子设备的干扰。

original.en: This applies particularly to chemical industries, where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
original.zh: 这种情况在化学工业尤其适用，在该行业中，偶然发现的作用要比在物理和机械工业中大得多。

imitations.en: This learning method applies particularly to language learners, where enough input is the key to improvement.
imitations.zh: 这种学习方法尤其适合语言学习者，对他们来说，足量的输入是提升的关键。

imitations.en: This regulation applies particularly to small businesses, where cash flow is more vulnerable to market changes.
imitations.zh: 这项规定尤其适用于小型企业，在这类企业中，现金流更容易受市场变化的影响。

patterns.pattern: Sometimes the ... goes to such an extent that...

original.en: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
original.zh: 有时保密的程度到了连研究的性质都不能提及的地步。

imitations.en: Sometimes the competition in the industry goes to such an extent that companies cut their prices below cost.
imitations.zh: 有时行业内的竞争激烈到了公司把价格降到成本以下的程度。

imitations.en: Sometimes parents' love for their children goes to such an extent that they arrange everything for them.
imitations.zh: 有时父母对孩子的爱到了事事都为他们安排好的地步。

lines.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
lines.zh: 有两个因素严重地妨碍工业中科学研究的效率：一是科研工作中普遍存在的保密气氛；二是研究人员缺乏个人自由。

lines.en: One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out, the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
lines.zh: 任何一项研究都涉及到保密，那些从事科研的人员自然受到了限制。

lines.en: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one, it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities, or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
lines.zh: 他们不能和其他国家、其他大学、甚至往往不能与本公司的其他部门的同行们进行有效的接触。

lines.en: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably .
lines.zh: 保密程度自然差别很大。

lines.en: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
lines.zh: 某些大公司进行的研究属于一般和基础的研究，因此不保密对他们才有利。

lines.en: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.
lines.zh: 然而，依赖这种研究的很多工艺程序是在完全保密的情况下进行的，直到可以取得专利权的阶段为止。

lines.en: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
lines.zh: 更多的工艺过程根本就不会取得专利权，而是作为秘方保存着。

lines.en: This applies particularly to chemical industries, where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
lines.zh: 在这化学工业方面尤为突出。同物理和机械工业相比，化学工业中偶然发现的机会要多得多。

lines.en: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
lines.zh: 有时，保密竟达到了这样的程度，即连研究工作的整个性质都不准提及。

lines.en: Many firms, for instance, have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries because they are unwilling to have names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking J.D.
lines.zh: 比如，很多公司向图书馆借阅科技书籍时感到困难，因为它们不愿让人家记下它们公司的名字和借阅的某一本书。

lines.en: BERNAL The Social Function of Science
lines.zh: 他们生怕别的公司的情报人员据此摸到他们可能要从事的某项科研项目。

questions.q: Why is secrecy particularly important in the chemical industries?
questions.zh: 为什么保密在化学工业中尤为重要？
questions.a: Because in the chemical industries chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries, so firms keep their new processes strictly secret.
questions.aZh: 因为在化学工业中，偶然发现所起的作用远大于物理和机械工业，所以企业把新工艺严加保密。
questions.hint: 见课文第 7 句：This applies particularly to chemical industries, where chance discoveries play a much larger part...

questions.q: What two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry?
questions.zh: 哪两个因素严重妨碍工业中科学研究的效率？
questions.a: One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which research is carried out, the other is the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
questions.aZh: 一是科研工作中普遍存在的保密气氛，二是研究人员缺乏个人自由。
questions.hint: 见课文第 1、2 句，注意 the one ... the other 的对称结构。

questions.q: How does secrecy limit the scientists engaged in research?
questions.zh: 保密怎样限制了从事研究的科学家？
questions.a: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one, it limits them from effective contact with their fellow scientists in other countries or universities, or even in other departments of the same firm.
questions.aZh: 只要某项研究是保密的，它就会限制他们与别国、别的大学，甚至本公司其他部门的同行进行有效接触。
questions.hint: 见课文第 3 句，注意 in so far as 引导的程度状语。

questions.q: What happens to the processes depending on such research?
questions.zh: 依赖这类研究的工艺程序会怎样？
questions.a: Many are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out; even more are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
questions.aZh: 很多工艺程序是在完全保密的情况下进行的，直到可以取得专利权的阶段；更多的则根本不会申请专利，而是作为秘方保存着。
questions.hint: 见课文第 5、6 句，注意 at which 引导的定语从句。

questions.q: Why are many firms unwilling to borrow books from libraries, and what does this show?
questions.zh: 为什么许多公司不愿从图书馆借书？这说明了什么？
questions.a: Because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking. It shows how extreme industrial secrecy can become.
questions.aZh: 因为它们不愿让人记下公司名字和所借书籍，生怕别家公司的情报人员据此摸到它们可能从事的科研项目。这表明工业保密可以走到多么极端的地步。
questions.hint: 见课文最后一句，体会 for fear (that) ... should 的用法。

translation:
有两个因素严重地妨碍工业中科学研究的效率：一是科研工作中普遍存在的保密气氛；二是研究人员缺乏个人自由。
任何一项研究都涉及到保密，那些从事科研的人员自然受到了限制。
他们不能和其他国家、其他大学、甚至往往不能与本公司的其他部门的同行们进行有效的接触。
保密程度自然差别很大。
某些大公司进行的研究属于一般和基础的研究，因此不保密对他们才有利。
然而，依赖这种研究的很多工艺程序是在完全保密的情况下进行的，直到可以取得专利权的阶段为止。
更多的工艺过程根本就不会取得专利权，而是作为秘方保存着。
在这化学工业方面尤为突出。
同物理和机械工业相比，化学工业中偶然发现的机会要多得多。
有时，保密竟达到了这样的程度，即连研究工作的整个性质都不准提及。
比如，很多公司向图书馆借阅科技书籍时感到困难，因为它们不愿让人家记下它们公司的名字和借阅的某一本书。
他们生怕别的公司的情报人员据此摸到他们可能要从事的某项科研项目。
title: Secrecy in Industry
subtitle: 工业中的秘密

lead.question: 工业中的科学研究为何效率不高？化学工业为何尤其需要保密？
lead.warmup: 想一想：公司里搞研发的人，为什么常不愿让人知道自己在研究什么？课文指出，工业科研效率受两个因素拖累——普遍存在的保密气氛，以及研究人员缺乏个人自由。保密把科研人员与外界同行隔离开来。作者还提到：公司连去图书馆借书都怕留下名字。读时留意保密到了什么程度、又付出什么代价。
goals: 掌握 secrecy、secret、industry、patent、inquiry、research worker 等科研与保密主题词汇。
理解 weigh against、in so far as、take out a patent、for fear (that) 等固定表达。
辨析 secrecy 与 secret，并熟练运用被动语态、such...that 与定语从句描述科研所受限制。
体会 the one ... the other 对称结构与 for fear (that)...should 所表达的目的语气。
lead.summary: 课文开篇指出工业科研效率受两大因素拖累：普遍的保密气氛与研究人员缺乏个人自由。保密使研究人员难与国内外同行有效接触。大公司的基础研究不必保密，更多工艺则在取得专利前严守机密，甚至永不申请专利。化学工业尤其如此，偶然发现远多于物理和机械工业，保密竟到了连研究性质都不能提及的地步。
lead.tips: secrecy 只作名词，指“保密状态”；secret 兼作名词和形容词，别混用。take out a patent 意为“取得专利”，动词搭配是 take out。for fear (that) 后从句常用 should，表示“唯恐”。

exercises.q: 汉译英：有两个因素严重妨碍工业中科学研究的效率。
exercises.a: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.

exercises.q: 填空：The degree of secrecy naturally ______ (vary) considerably from firm to firm.
句型转换：用 such...that 合并 “Some bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of general and fundamental nature. It is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.”
exercises.a: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.

exercises.q: 填空：Many processes are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage ______ which patents can be taken out.
exercises.note: at which 引导定语从句

exercises.q: 改错：Even more processes are never patented at all but keep as secret processes.
exercises.a: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.

exercises.q: 汉译英：有些公司不愿让人记下公司名字和所借书籍，生怕别家公司的情报人员据此摸到它们的研究项目。
exercises.a: Some firms are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out books, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.

exercises.q: 改错：Many firms have great difficulty to obtain technical or scientific books from libraries.
exercises.a: Many firms have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries.

quiz.q: 课文认为，严重妨碍工业中科学研究效率的两个因素是什么？
options: The atmosphere of secrecy and the lack of freedom of the research worker
High costs and a shortage of scientists
Poor libraries and slow printing
Tariffs and government regulations

quiz.q: 关于保密程度，课文怎么说？
options: It varies considerably from firm to firm.
It is the same in all industries.
It does not exist in big firms.
It applies only to universities.
quiz.note: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably.

quiz.q: 为什么某些大公司不把研究保密？
options: Because the research is of such general and fundamental nature that secrecy is no advantage.
Because they cannot afford to keep secrets.
Because the government forbids secrecy.
Because their scientists refuse to keep secrets.
quiz.note: not to keep them secret is a positive advantage。

quiz.q: 课文说化学工业的特殊之处是什么？
options: Chance discoveries play a much larger part there.
Chemical firms never take out patents.
Chemical research is never secret.
Chemical industries need no scientific books.
quiz.note: where chance discoveries play a much larger part。

quiz.q: 为什么许多公司不愿从图书馆借科技书籍？
options: They fear their names and the books would reveal their research.
They cannot read technical books.
The libraries refuse to lend to firms.
The books are far too expensive.
quiz.note: for fear the agents of other firms should trace their research。

quiz.q: 下列哪个句子的被动语态使用正确？
options: Even more processes are never patented but kept secret.
Even more processes are never patent but keep secret.
Even more processes never patented but kept secret.
Even more processes are never patented but keep secret.
quiz.note: 并列被动应为 are patented / (are) kept。
